A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, In-Context Learning and Occam’s Razor. All 21 pages of v3 and 24 pages of v4, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original regression, Mastermind, and HMM experiments, including architecture comparisons and the supplementary analyses in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds polynomial-model analyses in Figure 3 and a full-sequence versus suffix-loss experiment in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section C.3 introduces an interpretable variant whose bottleneck predicts Chebyshev coefficients and whose fixed polynomial evaluator replaces the learned MLP prediction head. The central prequential ICL procedure and existing architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 3 adds noisy cubic polynomial regression alongside a new probe within the existing linear-regression coverage. The previous sinusoidal regression, Mastermind, and HMM coverage remains; the new HMM loss-masking experiment does not introduce a new task.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds an evaluated suffix-only prediction-loss comparator against full-sequence training, using GPT-2-style Transformer and Mamba learners. Existing comparisons involving train-risk ICL, SGD and its regularizers, Transformer variants, Mamba variants, GPT-4, and the marginal-distribution baseline are retained.

E3.justification: The new polynomial experiment uses 20,000 functions, 400 training epochs, and a diagnostic measuring the norm of coefficients above the generating degree. Appendix G introduces full-versus-suffix loss masking on sequences of maximum length 200 while retaining the full observed context. These are additional protocols, not revisions to the existing experiments’ settings.

E4.justification: Figure 3 and Section C.3 directly inspect inferred functions and excess polynomial coefficients, substantially extending the evidence about model simplicity beyond prediction error. New Appendix G separately tests the importance of early-token losses. The earlier task-difficulty, regularization, and supervised-HMM analyses remain.

E5.justification: Retained experiments continue reporting standard errors over five ICL seeds and fifteen SGD seeds. No changed run counts, uncertainty estimators, or statistical-test procedures are documented. Figure G.1 adds a nonsignificance finding without specifying a new testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds findings that train-risk ICL uses larger unnecessary high-degree coefficients and visibly overfits noisy regression data. Figure G.1 reports worse short-context prediction with suffix-only training, but no statistically significant difference above 100 tokens. Existing benchmark comparisons retain their principal trends.

T1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 replace the joint data–model complexity argument with a data-compression and minimum-description-length argument. v3’s conditional model-complexity decompositions in Equations (5)–(10) are removed; v4 instead bounds conditional dataset complexity and argues indirectly for model simplicity. Appendix B’s derivation is also substantively rewritten.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claims that next-token ICL implements prequential coding, promotes simple models and low-data generalization, and remains vulnerable to underfitting and poor task generalization. The added experiments support these existing advertised contributions.

C2.justification: v4 interprets excess polynomial coefficients as evidence of overfitting and missing early-token losses as reducing pressure toward simplicity. Figure G.1 qualifies the latter interpretation at contexts above 100 tokens. Section 3.2 also softens its causal attribution of ICL’s advantage to consistency with the theory.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses GPUs with at least 32 GB RAM and runtime below one day per experiment on a single NVIDIA V100. Section C.3 documents the Chebyshev construction and new experiment’s training details. The code-access statement and existing implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Vapnik’s statistical learning theory and Mingard et al.’s work on neural networks’ Occam bias, and removes the auto-encoding variational Bayes citation with its ELBO analogy. It also softens the assertion that no known learner directly pursues the compression objective. Most other reference changes update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The central exposition in Sections 2.1–2.3 is extensively recast around dataset compression and MDL, with corresponding appendix revisions. v4 adds explanatory Section C.3, a new Appendix G, and an Impact Statement. The former Bayesian-perspective Appendix G is retained as Appendix H.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main-text layout, replaces Figure 1’s pseudocode illustration with a three-panel conceptual diagram, and separates v3 Figure 2 into Figures 2, 4, and 5. It adds Figures 3 and G.1 and relocates retained appendix displays. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 and Appendix G provide useful direct tests, while hardware disclosures and reorganized figures improve inspectability. However, the theoretical rewrite removes v3’s explicit conditional-model-complexity qualification, and v4 Appendix B asserts K(D,pθ) = K(D|T) + K(T) without justifying that equality. These concerns affect the central theoretical contribution, making the net balance of empirical gains and lost theoretical precision unclear.
